stats.title: Development stats
stats.description: How one iOS codebase grew month by month: code output, delivery cadence and features shipped.
stats.heroCaption: lines of Swift that live in the project today — excluding generated localizations and assets
stats.period: iOS app · SwiftUI + TCA · {first} — {last} · {commits} commits to main
stats.yoyNote: Two identical six-month windows: {base} vs {last}. All three metrics grew — the trend doesn't rest on a single number.
stats.recordNote: {month} is the project's record month: {lines} lines added.
stats.partialNote: {month} is excluded from the comparison — the month is still in progress (data through {date}).
stats.kpiBuildsSub: every commit to main is a working build
stats.growthSub: cumulative Swift lines (added − deleted), by month
stats.velocityNote: Monthly output. The iOS app is built single-handedly, so a rising curve reflects growing personal productivity — not headcount.
stats.buildsSub: every commit to main is a working build with a feature or fix · merge commits excluded
stats.featuresNote: Features are mined from ticket titles in the commit history — {count} in total. Each bar segment is one feature; the segment's height is the lines of code added on its ticket. Tickets whose commits are pure bug fixes are excluded, so the bars undercount the total volume of work.
stats.featuresChartSub: number above the bar = features shipped that month · hover for the list
stats.footAuthor: Author. Every line counted on this page was written by Dmitrii Cherviakov, the sole iOS developer on the project — pure SwiftUI and The Composable Architecture (TCA).
stats.footMethod: Methodology. Source — the git history of the main branch. Only *.swift files are counted; the generated Localizable.xcstrings (77k lines of JSON), assets and project files are excluded. The cumulative curve is built from git log --numstat and cross-checked against an exact line count at the end of each month — 0.3% discrepancy.
stats.footBuilds: Builds. The project follows trunk-based development: every non-merge commit to main is a shippable build carrying a feature or a fix, so build counts double as delivery cadence.
stats.footFeatures: Features. A ticket counts as a feature when at least one of its commits is not a fix; its size is the total lines added across the ticket's commits, attributed to the month where most of that code was written. Ticket IDs are omitted.
stats.footProxy: Lines of code are a proxy metric — sensitive to style and refactoring. That's why build counts and feature counts are shown alongside: the growth conclusion rests on more than one signal.
